result_text:
The drop is best explained by a new landing page, `/lp/summer-sale`, that started getting traffic on 06-08. It converts at about 0.57%. The data can't show whether the v3.4.1 deploy also hurt conversion. This is an association, not a proven cause, because nothing assigned who saw the new page.

**What the data shows**
- Your 3.1% → 2.5% matches `checkout_reached` ÷ sessions: 3.12% (131/4200) in week 1 and 2.51% (125/4971) in week 2. Orders ÷ sessions gives 3.12% → 2.76%, so the two sources disagree about the size of the drop.
- `/lp/summer-sale` had 1,053 sessions, about 26% of week-2 traffic, and only 6 of them reached checkout (0.57%). It didn't exist in week 1.
- Traffic to `/home` and `/product` converted 3.12% → 3.04%, essentially flat. Adding the summer-sale sessions to that flat baseline accounts for about 0.53 of the 0.61pp drop.
- The lower conversion shows up on 06-08 and 06-09, before the v3.4.1 release on 06-10. Summer-sale conversion was also the same before and after the deploy (3/427 vs 3/626).

**Hypothesis status**

| Hypothesis | Status | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New low-converting landing-page traffic | Unresolved, but best supported | The arithmetic fits, and the page didn't exist the week before. |
| v3.4.1 checkout refactor caused it | Unresolved | The drop predates the deploy, but only 1,520 sessions (37 orders) fall before it. A small regression can't be ruled out: on the existing pages, conversion went from 3.19% before the deploy to 2.93% after. The 95% interval on that difference is -1.36 to +0.86pp, so it includes zero. |
| Data or measurement artifact | Unresolved | The drop holds when 06-13 and 06-14 are excluded (2.55%), but those two days are anomalous (details below). |

**Limitations**
- On 06-13 and 06-14, mobile sessions fell about 45% and total sessions fell from 760 to about 587 a day, while orders did not fall. Week 2 has 12 more orders than checkout-reaching sessions; week 1 has none. I can't tell why, and orders can't be joined to sessions to check.
- The week-over-week change is statistically weak: about 130 orders a week, and the 95% interval on the orders-based difference is -1.06 to +0.31pp.
- I know nothing about the summer-sale campaign (spend, audience, targeting), so I can't say whether those visitors would have converted elsewhere.

**Next steps:** confirm what the summer-sale campaign is and check its traffic quality. Look into the 06-13/14 session-logging gap. Compare existing-page conversion over a longer post-deploy window before deciding on a rollback.

The working ledger is at `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s1-post-3-et6bed2u/work/ledger.md`. It passes the structural check, which says nothing about whether the analysis is right.
